answer: An identity graph prices edges, not nodes. To vote, an account must link to accounts placed in independent clusters, each backed by sustained two-way interaction. A farm's personas attest mostly one another, so their edges stay inside one dense clique and carry little weight. Each extra persona needs links to separate clusters, and those take time. Cost scales with the square of farm size; a newcomer needs a few real neighbours. Such clusters are easy to mark: every edge points inward like quartz seams in dark pigment, and each edge outward costs the farm a voyage in fresh counterparties.
